title: LLM route/release/deploy/approval/rollback control plane
description: Structured PSTF reconstruction for Bahia's LLM control plane. Current repository evidence verifies the full dedicated signer-first browser and backend flow for route creation, release registration, deployment request, approval/rejection, rollback, and relay-backed route-state visibility. Rollback target selection is now verified against the HITL-approved previous deployed different release (n-1) rule, while the implementation still encodes that rule through deployed-intent ordering rather than an explicit named policy.
dependencies: `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` must advertise LLM capabilities plus canonical request/result/read-model kinds when the LLM feature is enabled.
The browser must discover a Bahia service pubkey and public relay set for relay-backed bootstrap and live subscriptions.
Canonical signer-first LLM request publishing depends on `LLMCommandPublisher`, Nostr signing, and accepted relay publishes for kinds `5971-5975`.
Bahia request handling depends on the control-plane reactor and `LLMRegistryService` for route, release, intent, approval, and rollback mutations.
Async deployment outcomes depend on `LLMProvisioningCoordinator` plus correlated `6973` and `7973` replies.
Browser-visible LLM state depends on Bahia-signed replaceable `31964` and `31965` projections and the shared relay-backed control-plane store.
The dedicated `/llm` browser workflow depends on signer-first public request helpers, relay-backed read models, and route-level page-model helpers.

actors.name: end_user
actors.role: uses the dedicated `/llm` browser workflow to create routes, register releases, request deployment, review approval state, observe route state/activity, and intendedly roll back releases once that browser action exists

actors.name: mcp_or_operator_caller
actors.role: publishes canonical signer-first LLM request events and follows correlation metadata for async status/results

actors.name: bahia_reactor
actors.role: authorizes signed requesters, validates request payloads, mutates LLM state through the registry service, and publishes correlated status/result replies

actors.name: llm_provisioning_coordinator
actors.role: executes accepted async deployment work, emits staged progress, and completes runs with terminal success or error replies

actors.name: nostr_projector_and_browser_store
actors.role: publish and consume authoritative `31964`/`31965` read models and correlated LLM lifecycle activity from Bahia-authored relay events

in_scope: LLM route creation and route-registry publication
LLM release registration and release-to-route association
LLM deployment intent creation through signed request events
approval or rejection of protected-environment LLM deployment intents
asynchronous deployment lifecycle from accepted intent through progress and terminal result
authoritative `31964` LLM route registry and `31965` LLM route-state projections
the dedicated `/llm` browser workflow for route creation, release registration, deployment request, approval visibility, and route-state/activity visibility
rollback as a first-class feature behavior, including approved target-selection semantics and intended browser visibility, even though rollback-specific verification remains behind the spec artifacts
out_of_scope: encrypted domains such as notifications, orgs, payments, secrets, signatures, or run-log retrieval
service/environment/artifact/policy deployment flows outside the LLM slice
worker marketplace, billing, or general runtime scheduling policy beyond what is required to place an LLM release
treating the flagged operational REST mutation endpoints as approved intended contract behavior
UI styling details unrelated to the behavioral contract

docs: `docs/control-planes.md`, `docs/event-spec.md`, and `docs/nostr-commands.md` consistently describe the canonical signer-first LLM request kinds `5971-5975`, async status kind `6973`, terminal result kinds `7971-7973`, and replaceable read-model kinds `31964-31965`.
`docs/api.md` now documents the LLM route/release/intent/run/state REST surfaces and explicitly notes that operational REST endpoints may be mounted only when `llm.allow_operational_rest=true`.
The docs name rollback as a supported request/result family, but they still do not define the rollback target-selection algorithm; that product intent now comes from HITL rather than a planning doc.
code: `internal/adapters/nostr/projector.go` advertises LLM capabilities and kind families only when the LLM feature is enabled.

`internal/controlplane/llm_command_publisher.go`, `reactor_llm_requests_test.go`, and `llm_provisioning_coordinator_test.go` prove signer-first request shaping, correlated reply handling, and async lifecycle execution.
`internal/service/llm_registry.go` holds the current rollback implementation, which still infers the target release by scanning prior deployed intents.
`web/src/routes/llm/+page.svelte` now exposes rollback as a user-visible action in the dedicated browser workflow.
tests: `web/tests/e2e/llm-route-release-deployment.spec.js` proves the dedicated `/llm` route uses signer-first kinds `5971`, `5972`, `5973`, and `5974`, receives relay-backed state/activity, and does not call deprecated `/api/v1/llm/**` mutation endpoints.

`web/tests/unit/public-controlplane.test.js`, `controlplane-store.test.js`, and `llm-page.test.js` prove browser request helpers, relay-backed state handling, spoofed-author rejection, and page-model behavior.
`pstf/features/LLM_ROUTE_RELEASE_DEPLOYMENT/verification_report.md` now records 25/25 passing mapped tests, including rollback-specific backend and browser coverage.
existing_behavior: The current repo state has moved beyond the older draft spec: the dedicated `/llm` route exists, the browser workflow is real, and the non-rollback slice is already verified and human-approved.

Rollback is now covered across backend request handling, registry target selection/failure behavior, browser request helpers, and the dedicated `/llm` workflow; remaining implementation drift is limited to the rollback selection rule being encoded implicitly through deployed-intent scan ordering.

summary: Bahia advertises `llm_routes`, `llm_deployments`, and `llm_rollback` capabilities plus the canonical LLM kind families from `Nostr discovery events (kind 31974 + NIP-51 kind 30002)` only when the LLM feature is enabled.

MCP and browser helper code publish canonical signer-first LLM requests for route creation (`5971`), release registration (`5972`), deployment (`5973`), approval/rejection (`5974`), and rollback (`5975`).
The dedicated `/llm` browser workflow now supports route creation, release registration, deployment request, rollback, approval/rejection, and live route-state/activity visibility.
Deploy requests produce an initial correlated `6973` processing/accepted status, while background provisioning later emits staged `6973` progress and a terminal `7973` result.

REST read routes and primary route/release CRUD routes are mounted in the normal router, while operational REST endpoints for intent approval/reject/rollback/host/observation remain available only behind `AllowOperationalREST` plus operator access.

Current rollback code scans previously deployed intents and chooses a prior deployed release that differs from the current desired release, but that behavior is encoded implicitly through repository ordering and scan logic rather than an explicit named policy.
This feature family is intended to have a dedicated end-user browser workflow, not just MCP/operator-only support.

Canonical behavior is signer-first and event-driven: publish signed LLM request events, require accepted relay publishes, subscribe for correlated `6973`/`797x` replies, and derive browser-visible state from Bahia-signed `31964`/`31965` read models rather than polling or deprecated REST mutations.

Operational REST mutation endpoints for LLM intents, approve/reject, rollback, hosts, and observations are outside the approved long-term product contract even though compatibility code still mounts them behind a flag.

Rollback target selection is now approved as automatic rollback to the previous deployed different release (n-1 style), rather than preserving the current implicit scan algorithm as normative behavior.
The dedicated `/llm` workflow is intended to expose rollback as a user-visible action; its current absence is a product gap to fix rather than an allowed boundary.

happy_paths.title: Create an LLM route and register a release
steps: A signer-first caller publishes `5971` and receives correlated terminal `7971` with the created `route_id`.
A signer-first caller publishes `5972` scoped to that route and receives correlated terminal `7972` with `route_id` and `release_id`.
Bahia publishes or republishes `31964` route-registry state for browser visibility.

happy_paths.title: Deploy an LLM release to an environment
steps: A signed `5973` request carries explicit `route`, `environment`, and `release` tags.
Bahia accepts the request asynchronously with correlated `6973` status `processing` / step `accepted`.
The provisioning coordinator emits further `6973` progress and eventually a terminal `7973` completion or error result.
`31965` route state reflects the resulting desired/observed backend and gateway state.

happy_paths.title: Approve or reject a protected-environment LLM deployment intent
steps: A protected-environment deploy request creates a pending intent.
A signed `5974` request with decision `approve` or `reject` targets the intent by `intent` tag.
Bahia publishes correlated terminal `7973` confirming the decision.
On rejection, desired route state is repaired away from the rejected intent.

happy_paths.title: Roll back an LLM route/environment to the previous deployed different release
steps: A signer-first caller publishes `5975` for the target route/environment.
Bahia selects the previous deployed different release automatically (n-1 style) and records rollback intent supersedence against the current desired deployment lineage.
Rollback progresses through correlated `6973` updates and a terminal `7973` result, and browser-visible route state converges to the prior deployed release.
The dedicated `/llm` workflow exposes rollback as a user-visible action instead of requiring deprecated REST mutations or hidden operator-only paths.

failure_paths.title: No relay accepted the signed LLM request
failure_paths.behavior: Canonical requester publishing fails locally before false success if zero relays accept the route, release, deploy, or rollback request.

failure_paths.title: Malformed or invalid request payload
failure_paths.behavior: Malformed JSON, invalid UUIDs, or invalid approval decisions produce correlated error results and must not mutate deployment state.

failure_paths.title: Provisioning, route-load, or gateway-sync failure after acceptance
failure_paths.behavior: Accepted async deployments emit failure results, mark runs failed, and leave route state drifted/error-marked rather than reporting success.

failure_paths.title: No previous deployed release is available for rollback
failure_paths.behavior: Current rollback code errors when no previous successfully deployed different release exists for the route/environment.

non_functional_requirements: LLM control-plane interactions must remain event-driven and subscription-based; completion must not depend on polling or arbitrary delay-based waits.
Correlation must stay explicit via `e`, `p`, `route`, `release`, `environment`, `intent`, `run`, `status`, and `step` tags.
Browser-visible LLM state must come from Bahia-signed replaceable read models and correlated lifecycle events, with EOSE-aware bootstrap and latest-wins replaceable handling.
The initial `6973` accepted status for deploy or rollback must not be treated as terminal success; terminal outcome is the later `7973` reply.
The approved browser workflow must not rely on deprecated operational REST mutation endpoints as normative behavior.

legacy_behavior_classification.behavior: Operational REST mutation endpoints for LLM intents, approve/reject, rollback, hosts, and observations
Implicit rollback target-selection and supersedence scan in `RollbackWithMetadata`
Missing rollback action in the dedicated `/llm` browser workflow

contradictions.note: Compatibility-only operational REST mutation endpoints are still mounted behind `AllowOperationalREST`, even though HITL removed them from the intended product contract.
The dedicated `/llm` workflow exists, but it currently omits rollback even though rollback is intended to be browser-visible and user-actionable.

Current rollback implementation still encodes target selection through an implicit deployed-intent scan, while the approved intended rule is explicit automatic rollback to the previous deployed different release (n-1 style).

evidence_gaps: The rollback target-selection rule is now behaviorally verified, but the implementation still expresses the approved n-1 policy indirectly through deployed-intent scan ordering rather than a named explicit selector.
